Subject: Slow SSE generation / high p99 during 18:55-19:00 PT surge

Hi Michael,

We're seeing a sharp degradation on our Brightline staging cluster during the 18:55-19:00 PT window. Metrics from our side: p95 ~1.1s (normal), p99 jumped to ~9.8s, and ~5% of SSE connections returned 502/timeout. Throughput dropped while backlog in our client-side queue spiked. This started after a marketing push at 18:50 that drove a short burst of traffic.

Impact: several customer-facing chats timed out; we had to fall back to polling which degraded UX. Can you confirm this is on Redwood's hosted streaming path and share an ETA for a fix / mitigation?

Attached: our client logs and a short HAR. Happy to hop on a call.

Thanks,
Kara

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Date: 2028-04-18T19:23:47Z
Subject: RE: Slow SSE generation / high p99 during 18:55-19:00 PT surge

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Ingress observed a rapid token-burst distribution from Brightline's client fleet starting 18:50:40 PT.
- Continuous-batching queues built up on region-us-west-2-inference-pool-3; queue depth peaked ~420 requests waiting to be batched.
- KV cache thrash observed for that model variant (kv miss rate + rehydration) which amplified per-request latency once queued.
- Autoscaler reaction lagged due to conservative CPU thresholds; scale-up completed ~70s after initial burst.

Short mitigations we pushed (19:18 PT):
- temporarily reduced max_batch_size from 64 -> 24 for the affected pool (reduces queue head-of-line blocking).
- enabled aggressive request shedding for low-priority routes (policy: shed after 2s waiting).
- initiated model-variant fallback to a smaller quantized candidate for new connections.

Effect: p99 for the route dropped from ~9.8s -> ~3.2s within ~90s post-change; error rate reduced to ~0.9%. p95 stayed ~1.0s.

Next steps (owner in parens):
- Detailed root-cause: batching policy + KV cache eviction interplay (Rishi/David).
- Autoscaler tuning and predictive spin-up policy (Naomi).
- Longer-term: adaptive batching by tenant and burst-mitigation guardrails (Marissa).

I will keep digging into traces (attached quick snapshot). If we need to roll a hotfix to batching logic you'll be notified immediately.

-Rishi
Senior Infrastructure Engineer

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

Date: 2028-04-18T20:05:58Z
Subject: RE: Slow SSE generation / high p99 during 18:55-19:00 PT surge

Summary from ops side:
- Autoscaler settings were intentionally conservative for that pool (to avoid over-provisioning overnight). We saw scale-up trigger but on a 60-90s cadence.
- Rolling predictive spin-up (based on short-term rate-of-change) would have softened the latency spike.

Temporary config we've applied (20:00 PT):
- Lowered scale-up window to 20s for pools tagged "customer-critical".
- Enabled proactive warm-up for quantized fallback variants when rate increases > 2x over 30s.

I recommend we communicate the temporary mitigations to Brightline and schedule a short postmortem with them tomorrow. Also recommending a credit for impacted time window (suggested: 1 hour of host credits from our committed pool) — flagging for exec approval.

- Naomi
Head of Reliability Operations
